Environment: Python 3.14.3, SQLite 3.50.2, fresh venv from `pip install -e ".[dev]"`.
unanticipated_findings: The README's own verification command does not work. Following README.md:114-169 exactly (cp config/senders.example.toml config/senders.toml; export WEBHOOK_SECRET_ACME=...; uvicorn ...; then the documented curl) returns `HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request {"error":"malformed_request","message":"required header is missing or malformed"}`, not the `202 {"status":"accepted"}` promised at README.md:172. Cause: the example config sets `dedup.header = "X-Webhook-Delivery-Id"` for acme with no fallback (config/senders.example.toml:19), so idempotency.py:57 rejects the delivery, but the documented curl never sends that header. Repro: run the README's Instalacao and Uso blocks verbatim. Adding `-H "X-Webhook-Delivery-Id: anything"` makes it 202.

The `suppressions` table grows without bound and is never purged, in exactly the aggressive-retry scenario the service is built for. store.py:190-210 `purge` deletes only from `deliveries`; nothing anywhere deletes from `suppressions`. Repro: send the same signed delivery 50 times -> `deliveries: 1`, `suppressions rows after 50 retries: 49`. Then `store.purge(conn, before=<future>, include_failed=True)` -> `deliveries after purge: 0`, `suppressions after purge: 49`. A sender that retries a single delivery every 30s writes ~2880 rows/day forever, and the documented retention/purge story does not cover it.

`Service.run_handler` has no status guard, so replay silently re-invokes the handler on deliveries that already succeeded - duplicating exactly the work the system exists to deduplicate. service.py:177-219 loads the delivery and calls the handler regardless of `status`, and cli.py:120/146-148 feeds it whatever `--status` selects. Repro: accept one delivery, run `run_handler(id)` three times -> `handler invocations for the SAME delivery: [1, 1, 1] attempts: 3 status: processed`. `webhook-receiver replay --status processed` (a plausible 3am command) would re-run every handler in the retention window with no warning, no --force, and no dry-run difference to signal it.

Durability is weaker than the README claims, undocumented. schema_sqlite.py:13 sets `PRAGMA synchronous = NORMAL`, which in WAL mode does not fsync on commit. The service commits and then returns 202 (service.py:103-112, app.py:107), so on OS crash or power loss a delivery that was acknowledged with a 2xx can be lost - and the sender will not retry, because it got its fast 2xx. Process-level crashes are safe; machine-level are not. README.md:41-46 says only "persiste a entrega antes de responder" and the delivery-promise section (README.md:54-71) lists three non-dedupable cases and one lost-execution case, none of which is this one.

Three broken cross-references in the README, all pointing at an architecture document that does not exist in the artefact. README.md:99-101 ends "Detalhes, invariantes e arestas conhecidas estao no mapa de arquitetura." with no link and no such file; README.md:179-180 ends mid-clause: "A forma completa das respostas, do CLI e do log esta em" followed by a blank line; README.md:285-286 ends mid-sentence: "Mudancas que toquem verificacao, deduplicacao ou o momento da resposta precisam". `find` over the artefact shows no docs/ directory and no ADR files, though the source comments cite ADR-010 through ADR-014 throughout.

A test-only mutable global lives in production source. service.py:42-50 defines `_before_reserve` and the module-level setter `set_reserve_barrier(hook)`, called between key resolution and reservation on every single request (service.py:99-100). It exists solely so tests/integration/test_http.py:194-231 can force an interleaving. It ships in the installed wheel, so any imported code can install a callback that executes inside request handling, and a test that fails to reset it in a `finally` leaves it armed for the rest of the process.

Artefact hygiene: `webhooks.db` (28 KB, containing one real 'acme' delivery with idempotency_key 'entrega-1') and `config/senders.toml` are both present in the artefact root even though .gitignore lists `*.db` and `config/senders.toml`. The shipped senders.toml is byte-identical to senders.example.toml, so no secret leaked, but a stale dev database ships with the project and would be picked up by `uvicorn ... --factory` run from the repo root.

FastAPI's default `/docs`, `/redoc`, and `/openapi.json` are mounted and unauthenticated (visible in the ci.sh route listing). Because routes are appended as raw Starlette `Route` objects (app.py:149-159) rather than via FastAPI decorators, the schema is empty - `curl http://localhost:8114/openapi.json` returns `{"openapi":"3.1.0","info":{...},"paths":{}}` - so `/docs` renders an empty page. Not a config-inventory leak, but it is dead public surface on a service whose /healthz was deliberately stripped of detail to avoid exactly that (app.py:122-123).

Minor timing asymmetry the code's own comments claim not to have. signature.py:43 returns STALE_TIMESTAMP before any HMAC is computed, while a bad signature costs one HMAC per configured secret, so the two 401s are distinguishable by response time even though app.py:41 makes their bodies identical (asserted at tests/integration/test_http.py:102-107, which checks only `.content`). Low impact - the attacker chooses the timestamp and so already knows which branch fired - but it does not match the stated property.
